currentContext.expansion: Mach's expansion in FY26 is platform and footprint build-out rather than physical capacity. The digital transformation strategy is anchored by the planned launch of 'Mach Travel', a comprehensive OTA portal offering flights, hotels, cruise bookings, spiritual tour packages and visa services, described as 90% ready and in a testing phase pending launch; it is designed to convert a captive audience of over 100,000 annual travellers into lifetime retail customers. Alongside it, in-house GDS/IATA ticketing is fully enabled to eliminate intermediary margins, a Corporate Travel Desk offering one-click managed travel and policy automation for MNC, GCC and MSME clients is operational, an AI-powered delegate management capability covering predictive pricing, automated delegate communications and AI-assisted itinerary planning is in development, and a cybersecurity framework aligned to the DPDP Act 2023 is being put in place with an internal auditor appointed. On the service footprint, the Company has exclusive helicopter-based Char Dham and Do Dham packages targeting HNIs and senior citizens, and is a key distributor for Cordelia Cruises, positioning it for India's cruise tourism market. The Company describes itself as an asset-light MICE, travel and event management services business that does not carry physical inventory, and no plant, capacity or rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.risk: Geopolitical escalation in West Asia — further airspace closures and an oil price surge
risks.note: Graded Medium probability / High impact. Directly inflates international MICE cost and forces itinerary rerouting; the Company's stated mitigation is an intensified Asia-Pacific and South America footprint with domestic government projects acting as a revenue buffer.

risks.risk: India-Pakistan border tensions affecting Northern India MICE
risks.note: Graded Low-Medium probability / Medium impact. Northern India group movements are exposed to renewed border tension; mitigated by geographic diversification to Southern India, Rajasthan and Goa and by advance rebooking policies.

risks.risk: Currency — INR depreciation against USD/EUR raising international MICE costs
risks.note: Graded Medium / Medium. A weaker Rupee elevates the cost base of outbound programmes priced in hard currency; mitigated through dynamic pricing models, client cost-sharing agreements and domestic revenue hedging.

risks.risk: Cost inflation — jet fuel prices and hotel ADR squeezing corporate event budgets
risks.note: Graded Medium / Medium. Input inflation compresses the client's willingness to spend and the Company's own margin; mitigated by in-house GDS ticketing to lock fares, bulk hotel contracting and dynamic repricing clauses.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity breaches and data privacy exposure from the Mach Travel platform
risks.note: Graded Medium probability / High impact, and structurally new as the Company moves from B2B event management into a consumer-facing digital platform holding traveller data. Mitigation is an internal auditor appointment, a cybersecurity framework per the DPDP Act 2023, and SSL/encryption.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration in select clients or government mandates
risks.note: Graded Medium probability / High impact — the clearest structural risk, given single mandates of the scale of the Punjab Tirth Yatra programme. Mitigation cited is a 30+ brand client base and a Government Projects Division that diversifies the revenue mix.

risks.risk: Execution risk on large-scale government programmes
risks.note: Graded Low-Medium probability / High impact, named against the Punjab Tirth Yatra programme. Mitigation relies on an experienced operations team, a sub-contractor network and a multi-vendor logistics model. The same mandates also lengthen the working-capital cycle through advances and billing cycles.

risks.risk: Regulatory change — MICE-related GST structure or aviation policy
risks.note: Graded Low probability / Medium impact. Mitigated by active engagement with IATA, IATO and ADTOI and by diversified revenue streams.

risks.risk: No Risk Management Committee is constituted at Board level
risks.note: The Board states there is no legal requirement to constitute a Risk Management Committee and instead relies on risk considerations being embedded in strategic and operational decision-making under a Risk Management Policy — a governance structure worth noting given the scale-up in government mandates and the move into consumer data.

growth_optionality.body: Expansion into new markets, growing demand for travel and tourism, and increasing adoption of digital technologies

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising corporate travel demand, increasing globalisation of Indian businesses and continued investment in tourism infrastructure are expected to support long-term industry growth.
- Consumer preference for experiential spending has proven resilient despite geopolitical volatility; the global MICE industry was valued at USD 937.43 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 2,030.95 billion by 2034 at a 9.0% CAGR.
- India remains the fastest-growing major economy, with GDP growth projected at 6.5-7.0% for FY26 by the Reserve Bank of India and FY27 real GDP growth of 6.8-7.2% by most multilateral agencies.
- Government infrastructure emphasis — targeting 350 operational airports by 2047, a highway network beyond 2 lakh km and development of convention infrastructure — provides a structurally supportive environment for the organised travel and MICE industry.
- H2 FY26 recovery was anchored by the Punjab Tirth Yatra mandate, the New Zealand MICE contract, IFFI 2025 hospitality and the pipeline recovery of deferred BFSI and insurance incentive programmes across Bali, Kenya, Argentina and Mexico.
- Cost headwinds on international MICE: jet fuel prices up an estimated 85-100% versus pre-conflict levels, Middle East airspace closures forcing itinerary rerouting, Europe-Asia flight times extended by 40-90 minutes, and the Rupee breaching INR 95/USD.
- Demand redirection effects — Indian arrivals to Azerbaijan fell 70% and to Turkey 38% year-on-year, redirecting demand to Southeast Asia, the Gulf and European alternatives, and a demand pivot to Asia-Pacific after Middle East disruption.
- Management states that a diversified project pipeline and disciplined execution, together with operational efficiency, strong vendor partnerships and prudent cost management, allowed stable revenues and healthy margins through the disruption.
- Mandate from the Government of Punjab to manage the Chief Minister's Tirth Yatra initiative, involving the movement and management of approximately 1,85,000 pilgrims over multiple phases.
- Several government assignments of varying scale secured in a relatively short span, described as demonstrating ability to execute high-impact programmes with strong compliance and logistical discipline.
- Multiple high-value domestic and international travel programmes secured during the year, including large corporate incentive movements and conferences involving hundreds of participants.
- H2 FY26 book anchored by the Punjab Tirth Yatra mandate, the New Zealand MICE contract and IFFI 2025 hospitality, plus deferred BFSI and insurance incentive programmes across Bali, Kenya, Argentina and Mexico returning to the pipeline.
